parsed.explanation: The operative regime combines (a) an unenforced 1861 same-sex statute carrying up to life imprisonment (secondary factor), (b) a sustained, presentation-based police pattern—men dressed as women singled out for detention, harassment, beating and public humiliation without charge, recorded in both 2012 and 2014 (tier-2 state-tolerated targeting reaching any visibly trans visitor), (c) no non-discrimination protection and no statutory recourse for a visitor, and (d) a dated but damning impunity record: a 2004 LGBT killing, refusal to classify it as a hate crime, and the killer's alleged escape. Pattern evidence is 12+ years old; the 2025 report neither confirms nor refutes it. No imprisonment, extortion, facility rule or border screening is documented, and no subnational variation exists. Net: routine state-run outing exposure with beatings and no remedy, but no credible imprisonment pathway.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No passport-marker, visa, body-scanner or border-screening friction appears in the dossier; the only stated outing route is police attention to presentation in-country.
entry_documents.interaction: A document/presentation mismatch could hand a border officer the same presentation-based suspicion police already act on, but no border rule is stated.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police harass, detain, beat and publicly humiliate people perceived LGBT; men dressed as women singled out for detention and never formally charged. Recorded in 2012 and 2014, indicating sustained practice.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Detention ends without charge, but no complaint body, legal aid or oversight route is described.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Presentation, not conduct, triggers stops; the unenforced 1861 statute supplies latent legal leverage even though no prosecution is documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, ward, custody-placement or facility rule appears; the policing pattern and discrimination findings are stated nationally with no named localities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Absence of stated subnational variation means the national police pattern is assumed to apply everywhere, but this is thin rather than confirmed.

care_services.exposure: 2014 shadow report documents SOGI discrimination in health and education; resident-facing, with no visitor-specific care denial recorded.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing emergency care could encounter the same documented health-sector discrimination, but the dossier does not show it reaching foreigners.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Institutional hostility: police denunciation and humiliation of gender-nonconforming people, religious-institution hate speech, official/societal discrimination (2012), and refusal to classify an LGBT killing as a hate crime.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: The state is perpetrator and bystander; the life-imprisonment statute frames LGBT people as criminal even while unenforced.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. Nothing on travelling families, minors or guardians; documented health/education discrimination and community stigma are resident-facing and undated for children.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visibly trans parent or child would fall under the same presentation-based police attention, but the dossier does not address age at all.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police beatings of detainees; 2004 rape and murder of a lesbian activist, police refusal to classify it as a hate crime, alleged killer's escape from custody (2005). Dated single case plus sustained police-practice reports.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Killer was arrested in January 2005; otherwise none documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State non-response converts public violence into impunity; the case is 20 years old and proves capacity, not current rate.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No non-discrimination protection on SOGI grounds; a visitor has no statutory route of recourse. Unknown whether the 1861 statute was amended since 2012, and the police pattern's current frequency is unverified after 2014.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Not documented. No ombuds, tribunal, legal aid or consular mechanism appears.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of remedy means any police stop escalates without an institutional brake.

anchor_checks.comparison: Karthovia's unwritten police instruction to stop transgender visitors for identity checks, interviews and release without charge is the closest analogue. Ours is worse: documented beatings, public humiliation, no confiscation/fine/movement-order detail but also no review body at all, plus a dated lethal-violence impunity record. Ours is better only in that the pattern evidence is 12+ years old and no phone/passport seizure or administrative penalty is recorded. Sits slightly below 0.35.

Kestrel Isles exposes travellers only to administrative secondary screening, refused admission and slow appeals. This dossier's exposure is police detention, beating and humiliation inside the country with zero recourse—custodial and physical, not administrative. Materially below 0.55; refusal-of-entry friction alone would have been comparable, but state street-level violence outranks it.

Meridia has trained border officers, brief detention with written reasons, counsel access and a working tribunal. This jurisdiction has the opposite on every count: sustained police targeting, beatings, no charge, no oversight, no non-discrimination law. Far below 0.75; it fails the tier-3-plus test where remedies are shown functioning.

Varnalia's weekly raids, photographs, fines, extortion and multi-year appeals include custodial-adjacent and extractive harms this dossier does not document. Ours records no extortion, no raids on community venues, no fines and no imprisonment. Comparable institutional hostility, but the documented harm set is narrower and partly dated—so this rates a step above 0.25.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a presentation-based police targeting pattern layered over an unenforced life-imprisonment sodomy statute and total absence of visitor-facing recourse. What drives the score is tier-2 state-tolerated targeting: men dressed as women are detained, beaten and publicly humiliated without charge, recorded across two reporting periods, so a visibly trans traveller is exposed continuously regardless of conduct. The 1861 statute is secondary—no prosecution is documented—but supplies legal leverage. The 2004 killing with police refusal and the killer's escape show lethal violence plus institutional impunity, though dated. Offsetting limits are real: no imprisonment, extortion, facility or border rule is documented, detention ends uncharged, and pattern evidence stops in 2014 while the 2025 report is silent rather than reassuring. Silence is not safety, so the structural signals—criminalising statute, no recognition, no remedy, documented police hostility—govern. Adult-alone and adult-with-minor ratings are identical because the dossier addresses no age dimension.
